translations.text: There was a man named Tsirutsaydan, a lover of evil, who boasted of his many horses and the strength of the army under his command.
He had many idol gods before whom he bowed, whom he worshiped, and to whom he offered sacrifices day and night.
In the foolishness of his heart, he thought that they were the ones who gave him power and strength.
He continually offered sacrifices to his gods.
He also thought that they gave him authority in battle and in everything he desired.
He himself offered sacrifices day and night.
He appointed magicians for them.
They pretended and told him that his gods ate day and night, while they themselves ate from that unclean sacrifice.
And again they force others like themselves to sacrifice and eat; and again they themselves offer sacrifices and force others to sacrifice others like themselves.
But he trusts in his idol, which is of no use.

He imagines that they created him, since they feed him and make him king, because of the blindness of his heart and his lack of understanding. For Satan has blinded his heart so that he does not recognize the God who created him, made him, and established him when neither he nor his possessions existed, so that he may go with Satan into judgment, and they may be condemned with him forever, together with those whom he called gods, although they are not gods.
And it is fitting to call them dead, for even now they are not alive.

As for those who trust in them, whose [?] is dust, the children of humankind, the spirit of Satan that deceives them enters into it with their idols. It speaks to them according to the desires of their hearts and appears to them as they wish.

When they see that he has fulfilled what they intended, they marvel and carry out his will, even to the point of slaughtering their sons and daughters who came from their wombs. They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and daughters.

They do not recoil from them, because Satan has made evil pleasing to them according to their desires, so that he may bring them down with him into his condemnation, the [?] of hell, from which there is no escape forever and ever.
Now Tsirutsaydan was arrogant, and he had [?] gods in male form and in female form.
He boasted of those gods of his, although they were of no use, and honored them all the more, offering sacrifices to them evening and morning.
He made the people offer sacrifices, and he himself ate from that unclean sacrifice. He also made others eat, bringing still greater condemnation upon himself for his wickedness.
He built his gods a temple of cast bronze, iron, and lead.
He overlaid them with gold and silver and made curtains and tents around the walls of his house.
He appointed guards there and offered sacrifices to them every morning.
He thought that his gods ate, and there were libations of wine and a silver bowl prepared with sandalwood oil.
He said to his magicians, “Take it and give it to them. Let my gods eat from my sacrifices and drink from all my libations. If it is not enough for them, I will give them more.”
He made everyone eat and drink from that unclean sacrifice.

In his wicked delusion, he sent his troops to search throughout his kingdom, to discover and find out whether anyone did not offer sacrifices or bow before them. They were to bring such a person and punish him before the king with the sword and fire, plunder his possessions, burn his house, and take everything he had.
“I myself will subject him to suffering and punishment if he refuses to worship and offer sacrifices to my gods, for they are great and good, and in their goodness they made us.
They created heaven and earth, the great sea, the sun, the moon, the stars, the winds, the rains, and everything that moves, for our nourishment and satisfaction.
Those who do not worship them will be punished with suffering and distress, and they will not have mercy on them.”
There was a man from the people of Benjamin whose name was Maccabeus.
And in him.
They found them, and he said to them, “Do you not bow down and offer sacrifices to the gods of King Tsirutsaydan, as he commanded?
If you refuse, we will seize you and take you to the king, and we will destroy all your possessions, as the king commanded.”

These good young men answered him, “We have someone before whom we bow: the God of our fathers, the Creator of heaven and earth and the sea and everything in it, the Creator of the sun, the moon, the stars, and the clouds. He is the true God, whom we worship and in whom we believe.”
These were the king’s attendants, four princes, each with his troops, who carried weapons at their waists.
When they wanted to seize these holy men, they escaped from their hands, and no one touched them. They went away carrying their farming tools, for they were very strong and powerful young men.
Some of them kill a bear by strangling it, at times strangling it like a chicken.
Some of them kill a lion with a single blow from a stone or with one stroke of a wooden club.
Among them was one who could kill a hundred men in battle at one time with a single sword. Thus their names and their fame were remembered throughout the land of Moab and among the Chaldeans.
They were mighty in strength, and they possessed beauty, grace, and eloquence.
The beauty of their faces was exceedingly wonderful, but surpassing everything was the beauty of their hearts, because they worshiped God and did not fear death.
When they had frightened the soldiers, no one could seize them. These mighty men escaped into a formidable mountain.

The soldiers entered the city, surrounded its gates, and threatened the people, saying, “Unless you bring us these Maccabean men, we will burn your city with fire, send word to the king, and destroy your city.”

Then the people of the city came out, poor and rich, men and women [?], and children. They all cried out together, lifted their eyes toward the mountain, and called to them, saying, “Do not destroy us and our city!”
Then they wept together and received mercy from God.
They turned their faces toward the east and prayed to God, spreading out their hands together. They said, “Lord, we reject these transgressors of your law and your commandment.
We do not wish to listen to the words of that lawless man, who does not believe in your law, but in gold and silver, wood and stone, the work of human hands.
He makes himself like those who created him, although you are his Creator, who kills and gives life. But he sheds human blood and eats human flesh.
We do not wish to see the face of that lawless man or listen to his words.
Nevertheless, if you command us, we will go to him and surrender our lives to death for your sake. We will not listen to the words of that lawless man when he says, ‘Sacrifice to my gods.’
But we, Lord, have trusted in you with all our hearts, the God of our fathers who do your will and walked in your law, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who tests hearts and innermost thoughts.”
You examine the righteous and the sinner, and you search what is in the human heart. Nothing is concealed from you; even what is hidden is revealed before you.
But we have no other God besides you.
Only be our strength and firmness, and protect us in this work in which we serve you, so that we may save our lives from death for the sake of your holy name.
When Israel entered the land of Egypt, you heard Jacob’s prayer. Now we too ask you, holy God.
And when he appeared to them
The beauty of their faces [?] increased, and they shone more brightly than the sun and became more beautiful than before.

A voice came from heaven, saying, “Abijah, Silas, and Fentos, servants of God Most High, just as you have seen these people who died and rose before you, so you too will rise after your death, and your faces will shine in the kingdom of heaven.”
They went with those men and became martyrs there.
Then they prayed, gave thanks, and bowed down to the Lord. Neither death nor the king’s judgment frightened them.

They went to those lawless men and did not threaten them, but were like harmless sheep. When they reached them, the men seized them, struck them, bound them, flogged them, brought them to the king, and made them stand before him.
The king spoke and said to them, “You rebels, why do you not sacrifice and bow down to my gods?”
Those holy, blessed, chosen, and joyful brothers—Abijah, Silas, and Fentos, precious as a natural pearl of extraordinary value—answered him as though they had a single mouth.
They said to that wicked king, “We will not sacrifice or bow down to unclean gods that have neither a heart nor understanding.

Moreover, they are gold and silver, wood and stone, the work of mortal hands and the work of human hands. They have neither life, intelligence, nor understanding. They do no good to those who treat them well and do no harm to those who treat them badly.”
The king answered them and said, “Why do you act like this and insult my honored gods? They too recognize whoever mistreats and insults them.”
They answered and said to him, “We insult them and do not honor them, because they are nothing to us.”
The king answered and said to them, “I will judge you according to the wickedness of your deeds, and I will destroy the beauty of your faces through great suffering, flogging, and fire.”
And now tell me whether you will sacrifice to my gods or not. Otherwise I will bring upon you the punishment of leather lashes, ropes, and the sword.

They answered him, “We will neither bow down nor sacrifice to unclean gods.” The king ordered them to be beaten with thick rods, then with leather lashes, and afterward to be cut open until their internal organs could be seen.
Then they bound them and kept them in the prison within the place of confinement until he could decide how to kill and punish them.
They took them into the prison and bound them mercilessly with heavy bonds. They remained in prison for three days and three nights.
After three days, the king ordered a herald to proclaim that the princes, counselors, governors, and leading men of the city should assemble.
As King Tsirutsaydan sat in his court, he ordered them to bring those blessed ones, Abijah, Shelah, Phintos, and their mother, before him, bound and wounded.
The king said to them, “Have you come to a better decision during these three days, or do you still persist in your former wickedness?”
The blessed soldiers of God answered him, “We are resolute, and we will not say yes to the blasphemy you speak, which is full of wickedness and impurity.”
That apostate became furious and ordered them to be hung up and their wounds reopened. Their blood flowed onto the ground.

Again he ordered them to be burned with a hair comb, scorching their flesh, and they did so. The blessed men said to him, “Go on, Aresis! The more you increase our punishment, the more our reward increases.”
Again he ordered savage beasts—leopards, bears, and lions—to be brought and unleashed upon them without having been fed, so that they would immediately devour them, bones and all.

He ordered the keepers of the beasts to unleash them upon the martyrs, and they did as they had been commanded. They bound the holy martyrs with their hands behind them and also tied them to stakes that they had skillfully prepared.
The beasts rushed upon them, roaring, but when they reached the martyrs, they bowed down to them and greeted them.
They returned to their keepers, roaring, and frightened the guards. They drove them along until they brought them before the king.
There they killed five people from the company of the lawless.

Many were crushed against one another as they cried out in fear, until even the king himself left his throne and fled. With great difficulty they caught the beasts and took them back to their quarters.
And they came.
The martyrs answered their brothers, “We do not wish to flee after taking our stand to bear witness. But if you are afraid, go and flee yourselves.”
Their younger brothers said, “We too will stand with you before the king, and if you die, we too will die with you.”
Then the king saw from the roof of his royal palace that those blessed ones had been released and were standing
The king ordered the five brothers to be seized and put in prison until he could decide how to punish them. They put them in prison and bound them mercilessly with heavy bonds in the hollow of a log.

King Tsirutsaydan said, “These deceitful youths have wearied me. How stubborn the hearts of these men are! Their deeds are as wicked as their strength is great. Whenever I say that they will choose what is good, they make their hearts more wicked.

I will repay them according to the wickedness of their deeds. I will burn their flesh with fire until it becomes ashes and is consumed there. I will scatter their burned flesh like dust upon a great mountain, so that the wind carries them away.”

After saying this, he waited three days and ordered the holy men to be brought. When these holy men had been brought forward, he ordered a fire to be kindled in a furnace and in a great pit, and ordered them to put into it [?] of stone and materials to intensify the fire: pitch, papyrus, fat, wild honey, [?], and sulfur.
When the furnace was blazing, his servants went to the king and said, “We have done what you commanded us. Send the people who are to be thrown in.”
He ordered them to take the martyrs and carry them into the fiery furnace. They did as the king had commanded them, and when the blessed men entered it, they gave their souls to God.
Angels received them while those who had thrown them in watched, and carried their souls into the embrace of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, in the paradise of delight.

When that apostate saw that they had died, he ordered their bodies to be burned with fire until they became like dust and to be scattered in the wind. But he could not burn off the hair on their heads, and they brought them out of the pit.
Again they lit a fire over them from morning until evening, but it did not touch them. Again he said, “Come on, let us throw their bodies into the sea.”

They did as the king had commanded them and threw them into the sea. But the sea did not swallow them, even though they had placed heavy pieces of iron, large stones, and a donkey-driven millstone upon them. They did not sink into the sea but floated above the deep, because the Spirit of the Lord was upon them. He failed against them in every scheme he devised.
For days, eagles and birds sheltered them with their wings from the heat of the sun and brought them to [?]
They did so, and wild animals and birds did not touch their bodies, and their bodies remained
When they saw them, their bodies shone like the rays of the sun, and angels surrounded their bodies like a tent of light.
He deliberated but could not determine what to do. Then he dug into the ground and buried the bodies of the five martyrs.
They appeared at night to that wicked king.

When he awoke, he was afraid and wanted to run from one corner of the house to another, because he thought that conspirators had entered his house and conspired against him. His knees trembled, and he was afraid because he thought they would kill him.
Because of this he said, “What do you want, my lords, and what shall I do for you?”

They answered him and said, “Are we not the ones whom you killed and burned, and whom you ordered to be thrown into the sea? But you failed, because God preserved our bodies, for we trusted in him. Praise be to God, because whoever trusts in him will not be rejected. We too, who trusted in him, have not been put to shame.
He said to them, “What compensation shall I give you for the evil I did to you? For I did not know that this judgment would come upon me like this.
Now tell me how much compensation I should give you, so that you do not take my life by killing me or bring me down alive into Sheol.
For I have wronged you. Forgive this sin of mine, for your Father’s law is mercy.”
The blessed martyrs answered him and said, “We will not repay you with evil in return for what [?] did to us. The Lord our God is there to repay you, for vengeance belongs to the Lord.

But we have appeared to you to show that we are alive, because of the blindness of your heart and the deficiency of your understanding. Although you thought you had killed us, you prepared life for us.
“But you and your gods will descend into the punishment of blazing fire, where there is no escape forever.”

Woe to you—you and your gods, whom you worship and bow down to! You have abandoned worship of the Lord who created you, although you are spittle and do not know where he brought you from. Are you not passing smoke, appearing now and vanishing tomorrow?
The king answered and said to them, “What do you command me to do? I will do everything you wish.”
They said to him, “It is not for our own sake that we instruct you, but for your sake, so that you do not enter the punishment of blazing fire.
For your gods are gold and silver, wood and stone, the work of human hands. They have no soul, heart, or understanding.

“For they [?] kill and do not give life. They do not make things good or bad; they do not dishonor or honor; they do not impoverish or enrich; they do not wipe out or plant. Instead, they lead you astray through the spirit of demons, who do not want a single human being to be saved.
Especially to those like you, whose hearts are blind, it seems that they created you, although you yourselves created them.
For the spirits of demons gather, and devils answer you as you wish, so that they may drown you in the sea of fire.
But you must abandon this error and worship the Lord our God. This will be our compensation for our death, so that we may gain a benefit for our souls.”
He was startled, astonished, amazed, and afraid, for sharp swords [?].
He said, “Now I know that the dead who have become dust truly rise again. And I [?] as one who has been spared from slaughter.”
Then they disappeared from the sight of that king. From that day, this Tsirutsaydan, who was proud and arrogant, stopped burning their bodies.

He rejoiced in the error of his heart and in his gods, for they had led him astray for many days. He was not the only one who went astray; he also led many others like himself astray, until they abandoned following their Creator.

“They sacrificed their sons and daughters to demons, and they carry out their hearts’ desires: sexual immorality and marriage, which their father Satan taught them, so that they would cause turmoil and enter marriages that God does not approve.

“They marry their mothers and defile their sisters and relatives, and do everything resembling this filthy conduct. They defile their souls and refuse to turn back, because Satan has hardened the hearts of those perverse people.
“But Tsirutsaydan is arrogant and boastful; he does not know his Creator and boasts of his gods.
“How, then, does God give kingship to those who do not know him?” And he said, “Because he tests whether they will turn back and return to him.
“If they turn back and return to him, he loves them and preserves their kingdom. But if they refuse, he condemns them to the terror of eternal hell.
“A king should fear the Lord God in proportion to the greatness of his kingdom, and a ruler should conduct himself well toward his Creator in proportion to the greatness of his authority.
“Likewise, leaders, great men, wealthy men, and governors should obey their Creator in proportion to the greatness of their honor.

“For he created all creation. He is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who impoverishes and enriches, who dishonors and honors. There is no other God besides him in heaven above or on earth below.
“Raytawi became arrogant, and through a single gnat God made his belly swell from his feet to his head. He died through that little gnat.
“Again, Nimrod became arrogant. He had an iron bed made because of his great strength, but God struck him down too.
“Again, Nebuchadnezzar became arrogant and said, ‘There is no other king besides me, and I am the one who makes the sun rise over the earth.’ He spoke this way because of his great pride.
“God drove him away from human society.
“When he acknowledged him, he restored him to his kingdom. Who has disobeyed and exalted himself against God his Creator without becoming dust?
“Who has transgressed his law and his ordinance without the earth swallowing him?
“You too, Tsirutsaydan, want to exalt yourself against your Creator. The same awaits you as awaited them: he will bring you down from your pride and send you down into the earth of death.
“And beyond that, into Sheol, into the outer darkness, where there is weeping and gnashing of teeth, into the lowest depths, into a great and deep pit, where there is no escape forever.”
You are a human being, and you are earth. You who are flesh will die like the proud kings like you who left behind the possessions of this world.
But we say that you are a human being and not God, for God is the creator of heaven and earth and your creator.
He brings down the proud and raises up the lowly. He gives strength to the weak, and he gives weakness to the strong.
He gives death to the living, and he raises the dead who have lain in graves and become dust.
He frees slaves from slavery to sin and brings them into life.
O King Sirutsaydan [?], why do you boast of your unclean gods, who are of no use?
God made the heavens, established the earth, and created the great sea. He set the sun and moon in place and ordered the seasons and years.
A human being goes out to work, spends the day working, and labors until evening. The stars of heaven, too, are fixed in place by his word.
He counts them all by their names, and nothing happens that God does not know.
He commanded the angels of heaven to serve him and praise his holy name, and the angels are sent everywhere for the sake of those who will inherit life.
The angel Raphael was sent to Tobit, and he saved Tobias in the land of Raguel.
An angel was sent to Gideon to instruct him in how to destroy the Philistines. An angel was also sent from Moses the prophet when he brought Israel across the Red Sea.
For he said, “God alone led them, and there was no foreign god with them.”
He brought them up onto the heights of the earth.
He fed them with the produce of the fields and nourished them with honey from the rock, for he loved them greatly.
He also made you king over his people and gave you authority over four kingdoms, so that you would protect the people, shepherd them justly, and do the will of your Creator.
He made you king so that you would love the Lord your God all the more, for he exalted you above everyone and made you king.

It is right that you should love the Lord your God all the more, just as he loved you and entrusted you with his entire flock. Do the Lord’s will, so that your days on earth may be long and he may be with you.
He will triumph for you over all your enemies, establish you upon all your thrones, and spread his wings over your head.

If only you understood: the Lord chose you just as he chose Saul from the children of Israel and made him king over Israel, his people, while he was looking after his father’s donkeys; and he sat upon the throne with Samuel the prophet.
He gave him a greater share than his brothers and said to him, “Look, from now on I have made you king, lord of the land, over his people. [?] his people.”
Treat those who do good with goodness, and those who do evil with evil, for God has appointed you over them to put to death and to keep alive.

You are to repay those who do good with good, and those who do evil with evil. For God has appointed you over everything you desire, so that you may do his will, whether by punishing or by keeping alive.

You, too, must do God's will at every time and every hour, so that he may fulfill your wishes in everything you have planned and everything you have asked, as you serve before him. For you, too, are the servant of the one who rules everything, the one who is above.
No one judges him, but he judges everyone.
No one appoints him, but he appoints everyone.
No one defeats him, but he defeats everyone.
No one frees him, but he frees everyone.
No one enslaves him, but he enslaves everyone. No one can escape from his hand, for judgment over heaven and earth belongs to him.
Nothing is hidden from his eyes; everything is revealed before him.
He sees everyone, but no one sees him. He hears the prayer of the person who prays to him and accepts that person's prayer, for he created humanity in his image and likeness.
He feeds everyone from his inexhaustible treasury, for he is a king who lives forever.
And the kings wrote concerning him, “Justice, justice,” because he justly makes kings of those who do his will.

And he illuminates their dwelling with indescribable light, where Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, David, Solomon, and Ezekiel are, and all the good kings whose dwelling is bright because they did God's will. The palace is not like one on earth; rather, the heavenly palace is exceedingly awe-inspiring, and its pavement is pure, with the colors of gold, silver, and jacinth.
Its appearance surpasses human understanding and is exceedingly bright. The palace of the kingdom of heaven shines with topaz, emerald, [?], and [?].

And with every precious stone beyond human understanding, the palace of the kingdom is exceedingly bright. The Craftsman himself made it according to his knowledge. The palace of the kingdom of heaven has a pure pavement with the colors of gold, silver, and jacinth, green and yellow, and the colors of jacinth and [?].
And thus it is exceedingly beautiful and lovely, pure and bright.
He is clothed in righteousness and justice and endowed with kindness and mercy.
And there the water of life flows, exceedingly pure, like the sun; there is a tabernacle of light, crowned with garlands of Hermon.
And around his house are planted sweet fruits of paradise, each with its own appearance and fragrance, and a garden of vines, olives, and oil. Its fruit is very beautiful and sweet-smelling.
And if a person of flesh entered it, the sweetness of the fragrance of its fruit would make his soul depart because of the immense joy that came over him.
And there the good kings who did God's will rejoice. Their deeds and their standing are known in the place of everlasting life in the kingdom of heaven.

And he showed that, as in heaven, so also on earth: according to the greatness of their earthly kingdoms, and as people honor them and bow down to them, so in heaven they will be honored, exalted, and rejoice, provided that they did good during their lives on earth.

But those who are oppressive in their kingship and in the authority that God gave them, who do not judge justly and fairly, and do not rescue the oppressed, the foreigner, and the orphan, have despised the voice of the poor and needy.

And they do not rescue the poor and needy from the hand of those who oppress them; they do not feed the hungry from their provisions or give the thirsty a drink from their drink, and they do not turn their ears toward the cries of human beings.

They will take these people into the dwelling of Sheol, into the regions of darkness. As great as their honor was, so great will their disgrace and poverty become when that great day that God has made reaches them, together with his wrath. As David said in the psalm, “Lord, do not punish me in your wrath, and do not rebuke me with your punishment.”
But as for those who did not keep your law, though they were kings and rulers and held power over the world on earth—

In heaven there is one who holds everything, and everyone's soul is in his hand, and everyone's life is in his mouth. He gives honor to those who honor him and loves those who love him, for he rules everything and judges everything.
And he examines the heart and the kidneys, for he is the King of heaven and earth, who grants the prayer of whoever prays to him with a pure heart.
He breaks the pride of the mighty who make widows and mortals weep.

It was not by your strength that you obtained this kingdom, nor by your ability that you sat on this throne. Rather, he himself, by his will, seated you on the royal throne to test whether you could govern his people, as Saul did in those days when he governed his people, but disobeyed the word of God and the word of Samuel the prophet, and did not kill the king of Amalek and their people.

For God said to Samuel the prophet, “Go and say to Saul, ‘Go and attack the land of Amalek, and kill all their kings and inhabitants, from human beings to animals, because they have angered me by transgressing the law, worshiping gods, bowing down to idols, practicing their forbidden acts, and doing every impure deed that has no benefit.’”
And because they had angered God in this way, he sent him to kill them.

But he spared their king, many animals, women, and virgins, and [?] the young men. Because of this, God said to Samuel the prophet, “Since he has transgressed my word and has not obeyed my command, go and tear away his kingdom.”
He anointed David son of Jesse to reign in his place over Israel.
“And release upon him a demon that will choke him.”

“For I gave him a kingdom so that he would do my will, and when he refused to do my will, I removed him from his purity. But you, go, tell him, and say to him, ‘Is this how you disobey God, who made you king over his people Israel and seated you on the throne of his kingdom?’”
“But you did not recognize how greatly he had given you great honor and greatness.”
Samuel the prophet went to King Saul and entered his presence while he was standing at the table, with Agag, king of Amalek, on his left.
And he said to him, “Why have you disobeyed God, who commanded you to kill the people and the animals?”
Then the king became afraid, rose from his throne, and seized Samuel's garment. Samuel refused to turn back, and Samuel's garment was torn.
And Samuel said to Saul, “The Lord has torn apart your kingdom.”

Again Saul said to Samuel, “Honor me before the people and intercede for me before God, so that he may have mercy on me.” But Samuel refused to go back on his word, because he feared the word of God his Creator and did not fear a mortal king.
And because of this he struck down Agag, king of Amalek, while food was still in his mouth.

An unclean spirit seized that wicked man who had disobeyed the word of the Lord and struck his head. For the Lord does not show respect for a king who commits injustice, because he is the King of kings, whom no one commands.
There is no one who commands him, for he is the Lord of all creation, who destroys all the authority of kings and rulers who do not fear him.
He also took the kingdom away from Saul and his son, as it is said, “The house of David continued to rise, while the house of Saul continued to decline.”

And the Lord took vengeance on the descendants of the house of Saul because Saul had angered him and had not destroyed those who rebelled against him and angered him by their evil deeds. For whoever does not take vengeance on the Lord’s enemy is himself the Lord’s enemy.
And whoever does not punish a sinner, although he can punish him and has the authority, is himself truly an enemy of the Lord: he does not avenge the law of the Lord [?].
Even if you are a king, and even if you are a ruler, what are you? Was it not the Lord who created you?

He brought you into being from nonexistence so that you would do his will, follow his command, and fear his judgment. Just as you become angry with your servants and have authority over them, so you too have someone who becomes angry with you and has authority over you.
Just as you strike without mercy those who commit wrongdoing, so you too have God to strike you and cast you into punishment from which there is no escape forever.
Just as you compel someone who has not paid you tribute and has not brought you a gift, why do you yourself not bring a gift to God?

And just as you want people to fear you, why do you not fear the Lord your God? For he is the one who created you and made you king over all his works, so that you might shepherd his people and his flock justly.
Do not show favoritism to either the great or the small, but judge justly and uprightly, as the Lord has appointed you to do. Whom should you fear except him? Keep his ways and his command.

Do not turn aside either to the right or to the left, as Moses commanded the children of Israel, saying to them, “I have placed fire and water before you. Stretch out your hand toward whichever you choose.”

Listen to the voice of the one whom I appoint for you, so that you may hear his voice and carry out his commandment, and so that you do not say, “He is beyond the river. Who will bring him to me, so that I may see him and hear his voice and carry out God's commandment?”

And if you say again, “Who will go up to heaven for me and bring down that word from God's mouth, so that I may hear it and carry it out?” he said, “Look, the word is near you, in your mouth, and look, it is in your hand.”
If you have not listened to the scripture, you have not listened to the Lord your God. And if you have not kept my word, you have not loved him, and you have [?] his commandment.

You are destined to enter eternal punishment, because you have not loved his commandment or done the will of the one who made you great and honored you above all your people, so that you might shepherd them in your righteousness.
He made you exalted and head over all his people, while you remember the name of your God, who created you and granted you authority to govern the people with justice and uprightness.
As for those who have wronged you, whether you discipline them or show them mercy, remember the way of the Lord, set your mind right, and judge uprightly.
And when people dispute before you, do not show favoritism, and do not accept a gift from a man so that you will show him mercy and wrong an innocent man, for the whole earth is yours.
And if you do his will, he will prolong your days.
Remember that you will rise from the dead [?] and stand before him, and you will be questioned about everything you have done, whether evil or good.

And if you have done good, you will dwell in the dwelling place of good kings, in houses of light. But if you have done evil, you will dwell in the dwelling place of evil kings, and the Lord will not show respect for [?] your rank.

But when you see the greatness of your majesty, the array of your weapons, and the ornaments hanging from your neck, and look at your horses and the army under your command, and those who blow horns and play harps before you,

when you see all this, you become proud in your thoughts and stiffen your neck, and you do not remember the one who gave you all this honor. Is it not true that when he tells you, “Leave,” you too will leave?
And he will give your honor to another, because you have made yourself utterly blind toward the ruler who appointed you.
And there he will examine you, call you to account, and judge you. For death will come upon you suddenly, and at the resurrection there will be judgment, and people’s deeds will be investigated.

There will be no one to honor the kings of the earth, and the crown of pride of the rulers of the earth will fall. For rich and poor will stand together for judgment and justice, because he is a righteous judge.
In just judgment, the soul will tremble, the books will be opened, and people’s deeds will be revealed, and nothing will remain hidden.

On the day of the resurrection of the dead, the earth will return what was deposited in it, just as a woman cannot close her womb once the time for giving birth has come and what is in her womb presses to come out.

And can the clouds hold back the rain, so that they do not release it where the Lord has commanded them, and it does not fall? In the same way, it is impossible for the dead not to rise once the time for resurrection has come. For the word of the Lord brought everything into being from nonexistence, and the word of the Lord brought everything down into the depths.
And the word of the Lord will again bring everything out of the depths, as Moses said, “People do not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord.”
Now it is known that the dead live by the word of the Lord.

And again he said in Deuteronomy concerning those who become kings and rulers and those who do his will: “At the time of judgment I will take vengeance on them, and in due time their feet will slip, for the day of their destruction is near.”
And again the Lord said to those who do not know the Lord’s judgment: “Know, know that I am [?] the Lord. I kill and I bring to life.”
“I also punish and show mercy. I bring down into Sheol and again raise up into heaven, and there is no one who can rescue anyone from my hand.”

Thus the Lord said concerning kings and [?] who did not keep his commandment: “Keep my law and my ordinances so that you may enter my eternal kingdom, for the kingdom on earth passes away and changes from morning to evening.”
For the Lord’s cup brings honor and disgrace: he disgraces one and honors another.
He removes the one who does not do his will, and appoints the one who does his will.

And concerning the resurrection of the dead, listen, and I will tell you. They plant trees, and they produce branches and vine shoots, and they produce from them, for God brings forth fruit from where there is nothing.
Breasts from water and earth.
And the Spirit of God gives fruit among them. So also is the resurrection of the dead.
And wind also remained in its own place and became wind, and fire also remained in its own place and became the sun’s heat.
And the Spirit of God returned into the hands of its creator, and he places it wherever he wishes, for he has chosen a time to bring it back.
And he keeps the souls of the righteous secure in houses of light, but he shuts the souls of sinners in houses of darkness until the time when he wishes to bring them out.
And he said to the prophet Ezekiel: “Call from the four winds, so that they may come together and become one spirit.”
And when he spoke thus, at a single word they came together from the four winds.
And water brought dew, and the sun in turn brought heat.
And the earth in turn brought dust, and the wind also brought breath.
And God also brought the soul from its dwelling, from the place where he had shut it up. And at a single word they came together, and there was a resurrection.
And again I will show you an example that is close to you: evening comes and you sleep; morning comes and you rise. When you sleep, you are dead.
And when you wake, it is an image of the resurrection. Night is an image of this world, which is entirely darkness, and the whole world sleeps in it, because the darkness of night has covered them.
And the breaking of dawn is an image of the resurrection of the dead, for through it darkness is driven away and there is light throughout the world, and people rise and go out to their work.
And so [?] is the renewal of the world and the resurrection of the dead, for this world passes away like this night.
And when the sun comes and shines, it is a likeness of this world, as David said: “And in the sun he set a tent.”

And when he comes in the new world, just as the sun shines now, when the Lord himself comes upon it, he will shine in the new world. For he said: “A sun that does not set and a lamp that is not extinguished—the Lord himself is its light.”

And again he will raise the dead in the blink of an eye. And again I will give you an example from your food, which you sow and by which you live: whether a grain of wheat, a grain of barley, or a lentil, or anything produced by human labor that is sown throughout the earth—unless it dies, nothing comes to life.
And when it dies, its flesh is consumed in the soil together with its [?], like the human flesh that you see.
And after its flesh has been consumed in the earth, it sprouts, as much as
you see. It too, unless it dies, cannot come to life; and when it sprouts, it produces an abundant crop.
And God gives fruit within that crop which has grown, and clothes it with flesh, skin, and a covering.
And the leaves, stalks, straw, and chaff cannot be counted by you. But see how greatly the grains of what you sowed multiply.
Do not be foolish, but see how much your seed has multiplied. In the same way, consider the resurrection of the dead and how they will be repaid according to their deeds.
And again, listen as I tell you how seed does not change into another kind of seed. If you sow wheat, will you reap [?]?
Barley. And if you sow cumin, will you harvest [?]? And among trees, if you plant a fig tree, will it produce almonds? And if you plant a walnut tree, will it produce grapes for you?
And if you plant sweet fruit, will something bitter grow? And if you plant a bitter tree, can it become sweet?

In the same way, if a sinner dies, can he become righteous at the resurrection? And if a righteous person dies, can he become a sinner at the resurrection? Rather, everyone will be repaid according to his deeds and according to the fruit of his work; according to the work of his hands he will be repaid. And no one will be condemned for another person's sin.
A cedar of Lebanon is planted and produces long, large branches. But unless the dew of Hermon rains upon it, its leaves do not flourish; instead, it dries up and withers.
And the juniper too is torn up by its roots if the winter rain does not fall upon it.
Likewise, unless the dew of life comes down upon them from God, the dead will not rise.
The lowlands of Gilboa and the mountains of Lebanon do not produce grass for livestock and wild animals when the rain of mercy does not come down upon them from God.
The mountains of Gilead and the lowlands of Elam do not give green vegetation to the goats and lambs that graze there, or to the wild animals, [?], wild oxen, and deer.

Likewise, rebels and heretics who previously acquired rebellion and error will not rise from the dead unless the dew of mercy comes down upon them from God, nor will deceivers and sorcerers, practitioners of [?] and [?].
And those who practice sorcery and magic, and murderers.
And those who commit unlawful sexual acts, and the Athenians and Medes who trust in their idols, sing to them, and make music for them with drums, stringed instruments, and harps.
They act madly with their idols and commit adultery with the works of their own hands, which cannot save themselves and will themselves be condemned on the day of judgment, at the resurrection.
You foolish and feeble-minded person, do you think that the dead will not rise?
Do not think this way, for you will not sleep there when the horn is blown at the resurrection of the dead by the mouth of Michael, the archangel.
Mountains and hills will be brought low; rivers and depths will be leveled, and they will become a level plain.
And there will be a resurrection for all flesh.
Graves, and their bones have decayed.
Will they not rise together at the resurrection with their relatives? And their bones will not be mixed with the bones of the wicked, the deceivers, and the pagans.
And you too, do not let your mind go astray, saying, “How will the dead rise after they have died, those who are placed [?] in—”
And when you look into the graves, not a handful of soil is found. “And how will the bones of the dead rise?” You say this in the foolishness of your heart.
Does not what you sowed sprout? You say, “Indeed, what you sowed sprouts.”

And in the same way, the souls that God has sown will rise quickly, and their raising will not be hindered, through his life-giving word. For he brought humanity from nonexistence into true existence.
And again, from existence he returned him to death, and again from death he returned him to existence.
Indeed, God is able to bring him to life and raise him.

Hermon and its surrounding regions have fallen, and those who worship idols in Zebulun and Edom will then be brought low, because God has repaid them according to their wickedness and according to the work of their hands. Tyre and Sidon will weep, because the one who will take vengeance on them has drawn near, on account of their wickedness and their idols, which they made in their youth and did not abandon until their old age.

And for this reason God will take vengeance on them, because they practiced [?], impurity, sexual immorality, and idolatry. And the daughters of Judah too will be put to shame, because they did not stand firm in the commandment of God their creator.

Like yours, Jerusalem’s disgrace will be revealed at the resurrection of the dead, because she did not walk according to God’s law and judgments, but walked in debauchery and the killing of the righteous.
At that time God will search her with the lamp of his wisdom and punish her for all the evil she committed in her childhood and did not abandon in her youth, even into her old age.
And she entered the grave and became dust, like her forefathers, who went their own way and rejected God's commandment, so that at the resurrection he would take vengeance on them.
For Moses said about them, “Their vineyard is like the vineyard of Sodom.
Their vine branches are from Gomorrah, their grape clusters are clusters of gall, and their taste is bitter.”
Their wine is the venom of the serpents of the earth, the deadly poison of vipers.

This is your disgrace, daughter of Jerusalem, which was written by the prophet: just like the deeds and sins of the people of Sodom and Gomorrah, so are your deeds and your sins, daughter of Jerusalem.
As with Sodom and Gomorrah, so it is with your disgrace: their vineyard was planted in sexual immorality and pride.

No rain of humility and mercy fell upon them, but only rain of pride and sexual immorality, through which their vineyard produced nothing but injustice, oppression, strife, bloodshed, and forgetfulness of the name of the Lord their God.
They did not acknowledge their Creator, but only their idols and their evil deeds. They indulged in the work of their hands and entered into sexual unions with animals and males.

They did not acknowledge God through their deeds, because their eyes were blind so that they could not see, and their ears were deaf so that they could not hear or do God’s will and what pleases him. They are the vineyard of Sodom; they are the vine branches of Gomorrah, which bear no sweet grape clusters.
When they press their grapes, the wine becomes deadly poison, because from its beginning the vine was planted under a curse, and its sap appeared in its youth.
There is never any good in their vine branches, because their vineyard was watered with the dew of Sheol, and their branches grew strong in a scorching wind.
And when it bore fruit and was pressed, it became a source of corruption and punishment. It hardens the hearts of those who drink it and consigns them to cold, far from God.
And a dwelling place for the devil, because they walk in his evil ways. The vine of Sodom takes hold, devouring, and climbs into the mountains and into the trees.
She crowns Baal, whom they worship at the threshing floor, and sacrifices her sons and daughters to demons who know neither evil nor good.
They shed innocent blood, and into [?] they pour libations from the grape clusters of Sodom’s vineyard.

She also worships and honors Dagon, who [?], and sacrifices to him from her fattened animals and her flocks, so that she may indulge in their libations and their madness, which the demons taught her, so that she would sacrifice to them and do their will.

They taught her not to acknowledge her Creator, her God, who continually feeds her and builds her up, from her childhood to the days of her youth, and on to the days of her old age and the day of her death.
“I will also take vengeance at the resurrection, and her time will last forever, because she did not return to my law or walk according to my commandments.

Let her gods raise you up! If they are true gods, let them run with her into Gehenna and save her when I rage against her in my wrath and bind all her companions who commit sexual immorality with her.
I have made her disgraced in everything, just as she brought defilement and disgrace upon my house and my holy things.

She brought forth my name, which was invoked over her, as people said of her, ‘Here are God’s people and the house of the God of Israel, the dwelling place of the name of the Most High: Jerusalem, the Holy of Holies, the city of the great King.’
She boasts in me as though she were my servant and I her master. Yet she does not fear me and do my will as her master, but contends with me like a rebel.
She serves foreign gods who neither feed her nor raise her nor clothe her. Instead, their sweetness has become a deceptive stumbling block for her, so that they may lead her far away from me.

She sacrifices to them and eats their sacrifices. She pours libations to them and drinks the wine of their libations. She burns incense to them and smells the fragrance of their incense. They command her, and she obeys them.
She also sacrifices her sons and daughters, and she [?] in the work of her hands and the labor of her lips, because she burns for them out of love for them.

Woe to her on the day of judgment, both to her and to her gods whom she loves and embraces! With them she will descend into Sheol, to the lowest depths, where its worm does not sleep and [?] is not extinguished.
Woe to you, disgraced daughter of Jerusalem, because you abandoned me, who created you, and worshiped foreign gods!
I will repay you according to your deeds and take vengeance on you according to your insults, because you provoked me and intensified my wrath, and did not make your deeds good.”

I too will mock you and will not hurry to save you, because you rejected my word and did not persevere in my counsel: that you should walk with me and keep my commandments, and that I should be with you and save you from all who oppose you, while you kept the commandments I gave you and my ordinances.

You did not keep any of this, and I too mocked you. At the time of judgment I will take vengeance on you. Was it not I who created you? Yet you did not keep my word and my commandments, though I blessed you so that you would be mine.
But you withdrew from me, just as Sodom and Gomorrah withdrew.

I struck them in my wrath, for you are of the stock of Sodom and Gomorrah, whom I destroyed. I wiped their memory from the earth so that they would not persist in their indecency, because they provoked me, their creator, by going to a man's wife and having unlawful intercourse with males and animals as with women.

There is no fear of God before their eyes, from the least of them to the greatest. No one rebukes another so that he will refrain from doing it [?]. They help them in every evil deed and are filled with every injustice and lust, for their deeds are evil.
Every evil deed is established in their minds, along with pride, arrogance, and greed.
Because of this, God mocked them and devastated their cities. Some he burned with fire down to their foundations, and nothing remained within them. They perished and were destroyed forever.

It will remain until the day of judgment, forever, and until the great day of judgment, because they were bound by sin. He will not forgive them or have mercy on them, because they provoked me by their evil deeds.

I too mocked them. Likewise you, disgraced daughter of Jerusalem, will be bound on the day of judgment, for you will find no excuse when I seize you in my wrath. All your deeds are filth, arrogance, greed, sexual immorality, lying speech, and every path of error and stumbling that I do not approve.
I appointed you for honor, but you appointed yourself for disgrace. While I called you mine, you gave yourself to another.
I chose you for holiness, but you belonged to the devil. Yet I have not punished you according to [?] your deeds.

I will prolong severe vengeance against you because of all your failure to listen to my word and keep the commandments I gave you on the day I loved you. For I am God, who created you, and I will be angry with all sinners who are like you. On the day of judgment I will repay them according to their wickedness.
But I will condemn you along with them, because you did not keep my word and mocked my judgment.
O Sodom and Gomorrah, you have no fear of God in your hearts!

Likewise, Jerusalem, [?] will be condemned together with you in the fire of Gehenna, along with all who did your deeds. For together you will descend to the Gehenna that has been prepared, from which there is no escape forever and ever.
You and she, who did not keep my word and my commandment, will descend together into Sheol on the day of judgment, because you did not keep my word and my commandment.

But those who kept my word and my commandment—the righteous will eat what sinners gathered, and the good will divide as spoil what the wicked acquired. As God commanded, the righteous and the good will rejoice and be glad.
But sinners and evildoers will weep and mourn over all the wrongs by which they strayed from my commandment.
But whoever keeps my word and walks according to my commandment will eat the blessing and be honored in my presence.
Everyone who keeps my word and carries out my commandment will eat the blessings of the earth and will enter and dwell in the dwelling place of good and upright kings.
Tyre and Sidon and all the districts of the land of Judah, which now exalt themselves—woe to them when I seize them in my wrath, for they will be disgraced and punished.

The Lord said, “For from them will come an arrogant and insolent man, a son of destruction, an enemy of righteousness, who stiffens his neck and boasts and does not acknowledge his Creator. For I have made him an example of my wrath, so that I may display my power against him,” said the Lord who rules over all.

This Capernaum, and Samaria, Galilee, Syria, Damascus, Cyprus, Achaia, and the entire region of the Jordan—stiff-necked nations who walk according to their own will, whom darkness and the shadow of death have blinded. They do not turn to the fear of God, and Seblanius [?] has blinded their hearts. Do not obey that arrogant one.

Woe then to those who obey the unclean ones and offer sacrifices in their names, because they rebel against God who created them and become like animals without understanding. For that wicked one, the son of destruction, sets up his images in every place and rejoices in the work of his hands, in his soul's desire, and in every lust, arrogance, injustice, and deceit, and in everyone who practices sexual immorality, arrogance, and falsehood.
For it is known that in his days he will act in this way, for it is determined by God that he should do this.

The sun will be darkened, the moon will become blood, and the stars will fall from heaven. Every work will perish through the sign that will come in the last days, to judge the earth and everything in it according to the deeds of those who inhabit it.
And in the end death will defeat the enemy, because he exalted himself over God's creation and did as he wished for one hour.
After him there will be no boasting, for I will take vengeance, said the Lord who rules over all.

He too will descend into the punishment and judgment reserved for him, [?] the day he is seized in my wrath. For he will drag all who are with him into destruction, punishment, and ruin. For I am the one who brings out and brings into the judgment of Gehenna.
Let the mighty not boast in their might, for he gives power and strength to the weak, and in turn gives weakness to the strong and mighty.
Vengeance will be exacted for widows and orphans, because he is the defender and avenger of those who are oppressed by the hand of their oppressors.
Woe to you who boast and stiffen your neck! You think that he will not seize you or punish you in my wrath, as he said, “Why has the morning star, which rises at dawn, [?] from heaven?”
For in his pride and boasting he said, “I will set my throne above the heavens and the stars, and I will be like the Most High.”

You dared to do this in your pride, and you did not remember your God, who created you and made you with his hands. Why did you exalt yourself, only to descend beneath the lowest depths because of the arrogance of your heart?

Through your pride you were brought lower than all the angels who are like you. For they praise their Creator with humility of spirit and do not stray from his commandment, because they know that he is the one who made and created them. They guarded their thoughts so that they would not transgress or depart from his commandment.

But you acted wickedly in the pride of your heart and became more dishonorable than your companions. For you are the guardian of all injustice, debauchery, hatred, and strife, in which sinners like you walk, and the wicked who came from your creation and rebel like you. They walk according to all your wishes and commands, by which you teach them debauchery.
Woe to you and those you led astray! On the left you will descend together into ruin.

Children of God who were led astray by that rebellious deceiver, woe to you! Together you will descend into everlasting punishment, because you went astray like him through what he and his demons taught you.
Previously, while Moses, the servant of God, was still there, you rebelled against him at Horeb, at the waters of deception, at Mount Sinai, and at Amalek.

And again, when you sent spies into the land of your inheritance, and they told you, “The journey is long, and their fortified walls are strong and reach up to heaven; their gates are [?], and those who [?] dwell and live there,” when they told you this, you [?] and altered the word of the Lord, intending to return to the land of Egypt, to your grievous slavery.

You did not remember the Lord, who saved you from your distress, who did great things in Egypt and led you by the hand of his angel. So that the sun would not burn you, a cloud shaded you by day; and so that your feet would not stumble in the darkness, he gave you light at night with a pillar of fire.

When Pharaoh and his army frightened you, you wailed and cried out to Moses. Moses cried out and appealed to the Lord, and through his angel he guided you so that you would not encounter Pharaoh’s army.

But he brought them back in torment, for it says, “The Lord alone led them, and no foreign god was with them.” He engulfed their enemies in the sea all together and did not leave even one survivor among them.
He brought Israel on foot through the middle of the sea, and no harm at all befell them from the Egyptians. He brought them to Mount Sinai, and there he fed them manna for four years.

They mocked the worship of the Lord, although he had done so many good things for them, for they continually provoked the Lord. In the book of the generations of the fathers, he said, “The hearts of human beings are dust, and in all their deeds they rush into lust and evil. Not one of them desires righteousness, but only the gathering of wealth through injustice, swearing falsely, oppressing a neighbor, theft, and lust.”
They run toward this evil all the days of their lives. The children of Israel, who transgress the commandments of God, provoked God still more, from the first to the last.

Even though the Lord punished the first people, the descendants of Cain, with the waters of the flood because of their sins, he submerged the earth in the waters of the flood and washed it clean of all the filth of the sins of Cain’s descendants.
He destroyed all the wrongdoers, for he said, “I regret that I made human beings.” He destroyed them all and left none except

Noah entered into a covenant with the Lord that he would not again destroy the earth with the waters of a flood, and that Noah’s descendants would not eat animals found dead or flesh torn by beasts, and would not worship foreign gods, but only the Lord their Creator. He, in turn, would be their God, would not destroy them all together without cause, would not withhold the spring and autumn rains from them, and would give food to each of his creatures—to people and animals—fruits, grass, and plants. They, in turn, were to conduct themselves well in everything that the Lord loved.

After he gave them this ordinance, the children of Israel provoked the Lord with their wickedness. They did not walk as their fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob had walked, who did not depart from the commandment of the Lord their Creator.
But the children of Israel were crooked in their deeds, from the least to the greatest, and did not keep the Lord’s commandment.
Even their Levites, messengers, and scribes all transgressed the Lord’s commandment.
They did not abide by the Lord’s law and ordinance, which Moses commanded them in the book of the law, saying, “Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
Love your neighbor as yourself. Do not worship foreign gods. Do not go to another man’s wife. Do not kill a person, and do not steal.
Do not be a false witness. Do not covet another person’s property or anything your brother owns, whether his donkey or his ox.”
When he commanded this, the rebellious children of Israel turned to sexual immorality, hatred, injustice, lust, going to another man’s wife, theft, falsehood, and the worship of gods.
At Horeb too, the children of Israel provoked God by making a calf that grazes on grass. They bowed down and said, “Here are our gods who brought us out of the land of Egypt.”
They rejoiced in the work of their hands. They ate, drank, and had their fill, and then got up to dance.

Because of this, Moses became angry and came down from Mount Sinai, for the Lord told him, “Your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, have sinned and gone astray. They have made a cast image of a cow and bowed down to its calf.”
Moses came down with Joshua, his young servant, angry with his people. When Joshua heard the noise, he said, “Look, I hear the sound of battle in the camp of Israel.”

Moses said to Joshua, “It is not the sound of battle, but the sound of revelry over wine.” He went down and shattered their image, grinding it by scraping until it became like dust. He put it into the spring from which the children of Israel drank, at the foot of the mountain.
Then he commanded the Levites to kill one another because of the evil they had done before the Lord.
They did as he commanded them, knowing that reproach against God was greater than the killing of themselves or the killing of their relatives and fathers.

Because of this, Moses said to them, “You have forgotten the Lord, who fed you, sheltered you, brought you out of the house of slavery, and gave you as an inheritance the possession that he swore to your fathers he would give to them and to their descendants after them.”
Even there they did not stop provoking the Lord, for they rushed into every kind of evil and sexual immorality.

And they were not like their fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who pleased God by their good conduct from their youth through their mature years and their old age, so that he would give them both earthly and heavenly things that he had prepared for those who love him: here, a land of inheritance flowing with milk and honey, and there, the paradise of delight set apart for the righteous—what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived, which God has prepared for those who love him, for Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who pleased God throughout their lives.
But their descendants were faithless and wicked. They followed the desires of their hearts and did not listen to the word of God, who had fed them, nurtured them, and protected them from their youth.
They did not remember God, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt and saved them from work with clay and from bitter forced labor.
But they provoked him still more, and he raised up foreigners from around them, who rose against them and enslaved them according to his will.

At that time the people of Midian rose against them and mobilized their armies to fight Israel. Their king's name was Akrandis, and early in the morning he assembled a great army from Syria, Cilicia, and Damascus.

He took up his position at the crossing of the Jordan and sent messengers to Israel, saying, “Give me tribute in dinars. Otherwise, I will come to punish you, plunder your goods, take all your possessions, and carry your children away captive.
I will deport you to a country you do not know, and there I will make you woodcutters and water carriers.
Do not boast, saying, ‘We are God's people. Is there anyone who can overcome us?’ Is it not God who sent me to destroy you and plunder your goods? He sent me to gather up everything you own.
Were there any foreign peoples whose gods saved them, among those whom I punished, whose goods and possessions I plundered, whom I killed, and whose offspring and children I carried away captive?
I will do the same to you if you do not pay me tribute as I have commanded you.” And he crossed the Jordan to plunder their goods and livestock and take his wife captive [?].
Then the Israelites wept bitterly before God. They cried out and wailed, but found no one to help them.
Because of this, God gave strength to three brothers. Their names were Mebecius, Maccabeus, and Judas. They were handsome in appearance and mighty in all their strength.

When they heard the Israelites weeping and lamenting, their hearts ached. All the Israelites—slaves, free people, and mortal men [?], their priests and their rulers, and every family of Israel, men, women, and children—all wept and put dust on their heads, and their nobles wore sackcloth.
Those good and handsome brothers prepared to go and save them. They took counsel together and said to one another, “Let us go and give our lives to death for these people.”
They went out boldly, with their swords at their waists and their spears in their hands. They went prepared to fight the ruler.

They arrived while he was eating a meal. Mebikyus struck the ruler and broke his neck with a single blow while food was still in his mouth. Judah and Maccabeus struck with the sword those who were on their king's right and left.
When their king fell, they all fled and ran away. Their weapons pierced their companions' hearts, their bows were shattered, and they themselves were broken.
But those good and kind brothers escaped, and no harm at all befell them. The wicked were crushed among themselves, because God brought punishment upon them.

They fell and died, and they left everything they owned until they crossed the Jordan. Everything they owned remained behind. When the children of Israel saw that they had departed and gone away with their [?], they took their plunder for themselves.
In this way God saved the Israelites through Mebikyus and his brothers.
For a few days the Israelites continued to please God.

And afterward [?] they returned again to their wickedness, and the children of Israel ceased to worship God sincerely. He again afflicted them through a people [?] who harvested the produce of their fields, ruined their vineyards, took their pastures, and slaughtered their cattle before their eyes. They could not save them, because they were a people who transgressed the law, continually provoking God at all times.
The people of Tyre and Sidon, those who lived by the waters of the sea and beyond the Jordan River, Gilead and Karan, the Canaanites, Jebusites, Girgashites, Edom, and the people of Amalek.
And all the nations, in their countries, according to their tribes, their orders, their territories, and the [?] of their lands—all existed as God had ordained for them.
Some of them had good conduct and knew God.
Others had wicked conduct and did not know God, who had created them and made them his own, as they did through Ameneser, king of Syria.
For he will take away the wealth of Damascus, and the plunder of Samaria will be divided before the king of Egypt.
The mountains of Gilead and the lowlands of Gilboa, all Samaria and Patos in the land of Judah, and those who live in the mountains of Arabia, Media, Parthia, Siwsigya, and Cappadocia.
And those who live within their territories, people with broad shoulders [?], who do not know God and have not kept his commandment.
He will repay them according to the evil of their conduct and according to the work of their hands.

For the region of Caesarea and the people of Gilead and Amalek join together to oppose the city of the Lord—you who are full of righteousness, in whom the Holy One of Israel is praised, the God of Israel, the Lord of hosts, who sits above the chariot of the cherubim. Myriads upon myriads upon myriads stand before him, and myriads of myriads serve him with fear and trembling.
And [?] Edom and Amalek do not worship the Lord, in whose hand is the judgment of heaven and earth, [?] his holy temple, for they are a rebellious people who do not walk in righteousness.

There is no fear of God before their eyes, but only sexual immorality, bloodshed, eating sacrificial meat, meat torn by animals, carrion, and everything like these things. They are detestable and loathsome.

They have neither faith nor salt, for they are enemies of good and do not know God. And as for the way of peace, [?], [?] and strife, every unclean practice, uproar, singing, and entertainment, as their father Sabelianos taught them.

For he enslaved them together with his demons and teaches them every evil practice of his own: [?], strife, taking another person's property by violence, theft, eating carrion and meat torn by animals, and sexual immorality.

And everything like these things: going to another man's wife, shedding blood, eating carrion and meat sacrificed to idols, unjustly taking a human life, coercion, inflicting suffering, greed, and every evil practice that does not please God. Their enemy Sabelianos brings them this teaching to lead them astray from the way of God, who rules over the whole world.
But what belongs to God is humility, gentleness, love for one's neighbor, compassion for one's brother, mutual love, and peace with all people.

Do not show favoritism to anyone, or be robbers, oppressors, abusers, men who go to another man's wife, people who do evil and violence to their neighbors, or people who conspire unjustly to oppress their neighbors.
They quarrel, join themselves together, and swear together to do evil. They hurry to lead people astray, to bring them down into the condemnation of eternal judgment.
Remember that you are going to God, and that everything is in his hand. You will stand before him to be judged for the deeds you have done.

For in the same way, long ago, the children of the Watchers were wicked and arrogant. No one was greater or stronger than they were in stature and in the strength of their arms. Yet they did not keep God before their eyes or acknowledge that he was their Creator, who brought them into being when they did not exist.
Their fathers, being angels, used to offer praise with the angels in heaven. But when their desire led them astray, they descended into the condemnation of eternal judgment.

They took wives from among human beings, for God created human flesh for them to bring them into subjection because of the pride of their hearts, and to test whether they would keep his commandment and his law.

They, however, do not keep the commandment, and he brought them down into the punishment of blazing fire with the devil, their father. Because of them, human lifespans were shortened, for God was angry with the angels who sinned like human beings.
They drew human beings along with them and brought them down into Sheol under their own condemnation.
Formerly, the lifespan of human beings [?] reached [?] years. For human lifespans were shortened because the angels went astray with the daughters of Cain.
And God said, “My spirit will not remain with them, for they are flesh and blood.”

Because of this, our lifespans were shortened. Moreover, some die while they are still children, for our lifespans have been shortened compared with those of our earliest ancestors because of our offenses and sins.
But our ancestors lived long lives because they kept his commandment and did not provoke God.
They admonished their daughters to teach them, and they admonished their sons not to transgress God's commandment.
Because of this, they lived long lives in righteousness, since neither they nor their sons and daughters transgressed God's commandment.
When the children of Cain multiplied, they made lyres, drums, harps, [?], and every kind of entertainment and singing.

Moreover, beautiful and lovely daughters were born to Cain by the wife of righteous Abel, whom he killed because of her, for she was lovely. After he killed his brother, he took her, and that other woman was also his.
He was driven away from his father and took them into the lowlands of Kephaz toward the west. The children of that lovely woman became beautiful like Amon.
Because of this, the angels came down to the children of Cain. They did not remain even one hour before taking for themselves the women they chose.
Because of this, God [?] both us and them, for together they drew us into error with them through their transgression.
The devil also drew our father Adam and our mother Eve into his own error, deceiving them and saying to them, “You will become gods like God your creator.”

In their foolishness, they thought this was true and transgressed the commandment of their creator, who brought them from nonexistence into existence so that they might worship and praise his holy name.
Their Lord disgraced those who appropriated God's gift for themselves, and that arrogant one too.
As David said, “Through the sinner's arrogance, the poor person is burned.” For through the devil's arrogance, Adam was condemned by the righteous judgment of the Lord his God.
Likewise, the angels who went astray with the daughters of Cain drew us into their error. Because of this, the days God gave us were shortened in comparison with the days of our fathers.
But they did good, and no evil came near them, because they made their hearts steadfast toward God. They teach their sons and daughters not to transgress the commandment of God that they taught them.
But if they themselves act without telling their children or teaching them, nothing benefits them.

As David said, “They did not hide it from their children, but told another generation the praises of God, his power, and the wonders he performed.” Just as they understood, they were to teach their children to understand and act, and entrust God's judgments to them, so that they would keep his commandments like their fathers, who pleased God by their good conduct.
They did not abandon his commandments, which their fathers entrusted to them in their youth—the fear of God and his judgments—as they themselves had been taught by their fathers.
Their children, too, were taught by their fathers to make their conduct good and to [?] praise to their Creator, because they kept his commandments and loved him.
He also hears their prayers and does not [?] their petitions, for he is merciful.
He often turns away his anger and does not kindle all his wrath.
Remember, our brothers, and do not forget what they told you before: God preserves the righteousness of those who do good.
Their offspring will increase upon the earth, and their memory will remain good forever. Their seed will not cease to bear grain upon the earth.
He saves them from the hands of all their adversaries and enemies who pursue them, because he contends on their behalf and does not abandon them into their enemies' hands.
He becomes a helper in their distress to those who love his name and take refuge in him, and he forgives all their sins.
David trusted in God, and God became his stronghold because he trusted in him, and saved him from the hand of King Saul.

And in the time of his son Absalom, and in the time of the Philistines, and in the time of the Amalekites and Edomites, and from [?]—God saved David from all these who opposed him, because he trusted in him and kept his law.
But God does not save the wicked kings who did not trust in him, for they were defeated by their enemies, because victory comes from God.
Hezekiah trusted in God, and he saved him from the hand of the arrogant Syrian.

But his son Manasseh was defeated by his enemy because he did not put his trust in God. Those enemies who defeated Manasseh were not like him, yet they bound him and took him to their country, because he did not put his trust in God or fear the one who honored him, exalted him, and made him great.

Then he was deprived of the wealth that God had given him, because he did not make his ways good before the Lord his God, so that God would prolong his days, oppose his enemy for him, and be his strength, firmness, completeness, and shelter.
For trusting in God is better than having a great army, and better than trusting in horses, shields, and bows.
For whoever trusts in God will live, be honored, and be exalted still more.
But those who did not trust in God and trusted instead in the abundance of their wealth were deprived of the grace he had given them, for God shows no favoritism.

He protects those who trust in him. But those who treat him foolishly, he makes foolish, and he does not hasten to help them in their distress when their enemies oppose them, because they do not make their hearts steadfast in following God and keeping God's commandments.
But for the one who is steadfast in following God, following his commandments, and keeping his law, he becomes that person's stronghold in his distress.

He makes him rejoice in the killing of his enemy, in the capture of his enemies' cattle, in taking his enemy's country captive, in the rains of its rainy seasons, in the produce of its crops, in the abundance of its grain heaps, and in the fruit of its gardens.
And in what grows in spring and autumn, in grass and green plants, and in its [?], so that your people who are under your hand may rejoice.

They will eat the fruit of another's labor and be filled with the rich food from their enemies—with animals, cattle, and sheep. They will eat the fruit of another's labor and take their enemies' children captive.
God does this for the one he loves, but the one he hates he makes a captive of his enemy.

He will bind his hands and feet, hand him over to his enemy, and make him a mockery to his enemies. He will not let him rejoice in the offspring of his household, because he violated God's commandment and shed blood.
He will not stand in judgment. He will repay those who do evil, the evildoers, with the fruit of their deeds when he punishes evil.
As for those who do good, he was commanded by God to repay them with good things and to protect them by his own hand.

He too must keep the commandment, for he is a messenger over everything that God created, to do good and give them eternal life. They praise God, who created them. Of all that he created, none transgresses his commandment except human beings alone.
They all acknowledge him and observe his commandment and his order, just as God commanded all of them to remain in their appointed order.
But the human being transgresses against the one who made him king over all the wild animals and livestock, and over all the birds that God created.

Whether in the sea or on dry land, everything God created he entrusted to our father Adam, so that he might do as he wished, eat them as he ate the plants of the earth, possess them, and make them serve him.
