Whether wild animals or livestock, God gave them over to obey human beings. And the human beings who were made kings were to obey God: because he gave them honor and appointed them over everything he created, they were to be faithful to him and obey him.
But if they depart from his commandment, he will strip them of the wealth he gave them and give it back to someone who does his will, for he is the ruler of heaven and earth.
He appoints whomever he wishes and removes whomever he wishes. He kills and gives life; he punishes and shows mercy.
There is no other like him, and no one can compel him, for he is the Lord of everything he created. There is no other God besides him, in heaven above or on earth below.
He appoints and removes; he kills and gives life; he punishes and shows mercy; he makes poor and makes rich.
He accepts the petitions of those who ask him and of the one who does his will with a pure heart. He hears their prayers and fulfills their wishes in everything they ask of him.
He places under their command the small and the great, and everything belonging to them in the mountains, hills, caves, forests, and the expanse of the earth, the sea, and the dry land.
Everything belongs to those who do the will of their God. He does not deprive them of his blessing, and he gives them the reward for their praise.
In heaven too, he gives them the honor he prepared for their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, David, Hezekiah, and Samuel, who depart from the commandment and judgment of the Lord.
So that he may give them the inheritance he swore to their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who pleased him from ancient times, and so that they may rejoice in his kingdom.
Remember, then, the names of those who do good, and do not forget their deeds.
Strive to make your name like theirs, so that you may rejoice with them in heaven, in the dwelling of light he prepared for the good kings and rulers who did the will of the Lord.
Also learn and inquire about the names of wicked kings and rulers, and how they are condemned and spoken ill of among people after their death.
In heaven too, they are condemned with the wicked and rebellious who did not do the will of the Lord, because, although they saw and heard, they did not make their ways good.
But you must not walk in the way of the wicked, whom the Lord has rejected because of their evil deeds. Instead, be good, innocent, and upright.
Judge justly, uphold the rights of the poor and the orphan, and rescue them from the hands of the sinners who oppress them.

Stand up for the orphan like a father, so that you may rescue him from the hand of his oppressor. Tremble within yourself when the orphan's tears are poured out, so that you will not tremble in the sea of fire where sinners who have not repented are condemned.
Direct your feet along the path of peace. Seek peace and pursue it, for the eyes of the Lord are upon his righteous people, and his ears are attentive to their prayers.
But God's wrath is against those who do evil, to erase their memory from the earth. He will leave no one who boasts [?], either in the mountains or in resting places.
My face will not turn away until I destroy those who do not keep my word, for I am the jealous Lord, who takes vengeance on those who hate me and those who have not kept my word.
I will honor those who honor me and keep my word.
Do not walk in the way of Cain, who killed his brother, who innocently followed him, thinking that his brother loved him.
He killed his brother out of jealousy over a woman. Those who commit injustice, jealousy, and deceit against their neighbors are like him.
They have walked in the way of Cain, not in the way of innocent Abel. For Abel [?] was innocent like a lamb, and his blood was like the blood of a pure lamb offered to the Lord with a pure heart.
But those who walk in the way of innocent Abel love the Lord, for they have become innocent like Abel. The Lord loves everyone who walks in innocence, as he loved righteous and innocent Abel.

But the Lord will put the wicked to shame. Their sentence is fixed upon their necks and written upon their shoulders, and they will read it on the day of judgment before angels, people, and all creation.
Then the rebellious and unjust who did not do the will of the Lord will be ashamed.
A fearful command will be pronounced against them, saying, “Cast them into the punishment of blazing fire, where there is no escape forever.”
But when Gideon trusted in the Lord, with a small army he defeated [?] and tens of thousands of troops, who were beyond counting, like locusts and swarms of [?].
Do not trust in foreign gods, for there is no other God besides me, O kings and rulers.
For I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of your mother's womb, made you grow, fed you, and clothed you. Why do you make excuses and worship another god besides me?

I did all this for you. What have you given me? And what do I desire from you except the salvation of your souls [?], that you should walk according to my law, my ordinances, and my commandments? And I too will give you the salvation of your souls.
God, who rules everything, said, “Save yourselves from idols, magicians, and diviners.”

For because of them the scourge of the Lord will come upon those who do this, upon those who listen to them, upon those who carry out their wishes, upon those who befriend them, and upon those who follow their commands.

For a people who do not know you and will not have mercy on you will rise against you and eat the fruit of your trees, if you do not do the will of the Lord who acted for you, as his prophets declared, beginning with Samuel the prophet. Ezekiel and Enoch also spoke, and Asaph [?].

And he said: Men who plunder [?] will come, changing their clothes. There is no other law among them except eating, drinking, adorning themselves with gold and silver, and every act of plunder that does not please the Lord.

They are ready to rush into eating and drinking as soon as they wake from their sleep. From morning until evening they rush into evil deeds. There is no path of peace for their feet; instead, misery and destruction are on their paths.

They do not know the path of peace, and there is no fear of the Lord before their eyes. They are a crooked and rapacious people, with neither salt nor faith: greedy people, gluttons, drinkers, and drunkards. Their sin is lawless, in marriage, bloodshed, theft, robbery, and violently taking another person's possessions.
They are accusers without law or justice, and there is no fear on their faces, because they do not fear the Lord who created them.

They show no respect for the person they see, for a gray-haired person, or for an elder. As soon as they hear of worldly possessions, they make them their own without seeing them with their eyes. And as soon as they see them with their eyes, it seems to them that they have swallowed them with their mouths, for there is no fear of the Lord before their eyes.
Their rulers too devour bribes. What they say in the morning they do not repeat in the evening, because they are treacherous, and there is therefore no honesty in their mouths.
Their kings too are troublemakers who rush to do evil, for they disregard the cries of the poor and needy and do not rescue foreigners from the hands of those who abuse them.
For this reason, kings must not be deaf, but must [?] the stranger and the oppressed.

They are [?] and rebels who drink blood and show no mercy to a young animal with its mother or to a bird with its young, for their way is plunder. Everything they see and everything that flourishes they make their own.

They show no mercy to the poor and needy. Instead, they love to gather things for themselves and violently take another person's possessions. Everything they find they collect, to store it in their houses and rejoice in it.

Woe to their souls when God seizes them in his wrath because they did not set their conduct right during their lives! They will perish quickly, like someone who leaves his hiding place, whose tracks cannot be found, and who does not return to his house.

In the same way they will perish together, [?]. When the Lord contends with them, they will come to an end at his appointed time. For the Lord does not hurry to destroy, but is patient to see whether they will turn to repentance.
If they do not turn to repentance, the Lord will destroy them like the earlier people who came before them, who did not keep the Lord's commandment with purity.

They eat human flesh and drink blood, and at no time is there fear of the Lord. For they gird themselves with oppression, ready to run as soon as they rise from their beds, and they do not cease doing injustice.
They eat and drink and rush into evil and destruction, so that they may ruin the lives of many on the earth.
Woe to their souls when I seize them in my wrath, says the Lord who rules everything, for their way is crooked, and everything they follow is on the path of Satan the deceiver.
They do not know the way of the Lord. They have cast it behind their backs and turned a blind eye to my law.

I too will repay them according to the evil of their deeds. At the last, on the day of judgment, I will take vengeance on them according to the evil deeds recorded before me. They will not escape from my hand, for I am the Lord who kills and gives life, who scourges and shows mercy.

There is no one who can escape from my hand, neither beneath the earth nor in the heights of heaven, nor in the sea or the depths of the waters. For I am the Lord from one end of the world to the other, and every soul is in my hand.
I command the serpent beneath the earth, the [?] in the sea, the birds in the air, and the creeping creatures in the wilderness. From one end to the other, and to the ends of the world, it is mine.

There is no one who can escape from my hand, in heaven above or on earth below, for I am the one who performs wonders and signs before my eyes. There is no one who says to me, 'Where are you going, and what are you doing?'
I command the angels and rulers above, and every name that is named is mine. All the birds of heaven, the wild animals of the wilderness, and the livestock are mine.
The south wind and the heat of summer will rise, and the Red Sea will roar because of the great majesty of the one who will come to it in the last days.
For he will judge the living and the dead, together with Nubia, Sheba, Ethiopia, India, and all their regions and borders.
He will shepherd them all gently with the staff in his hand, and with his staff he will shepherd his sheep, for his staff is higher than every other staff.
His horn is mightier than every other horn, and his kingdom is higher than every other kingdom. His authority encompasses the whole world; he can do everything, and nothing is beyond his power.
He commands the clouds above him, makes grass grow for the animals below him, and gives fruit to the crops.

He feeds all as he wills, each according to its kind, its fruit, and its food—all that he created: the [?] and frogs beneath the earth, and the wild beasts and livestock above the earth. He grants the prayer of the one who prays, and he does not reject the requests of the [?] and mortal human beings.
Still more does he accept the prayers of the pure, who pray to him at all times. For the songs of the wicked are like a storm wind, and the assembly of the unjust is like a drifting cloud.

Their joy, too, is like a bird in flight, and the beauty of their appearance, of gold and silver upon the earth, passes away. Their gold does not benefit them; rather, it is the [?] of the wicked, and their wealth of clothing is eaten by moths.

Their stores of grain and their clothing will be consumed [?] by moths and worms. Everything passes away like yesterday, the day that has passed. As a word that has come out of the mouth does not return, so is the wealth of sinners. As a shadow passes away, so does the splendor of their possessions. Like a worn-out garment, so is the wealth of sinners before God.

But as for the righteous, even if they are wealthy, God does not disregard them, because they show compassion to the poor with their wealth, uphold justice for orphans and the needy, clothe the naked from their own clothing, and do not withhold the produce of their household that God gave them to give to foreigners and the needy.

They must not pervert justice for the faithful, withhold a hired worker's wages, or commit injustice in the reckoning of their months or in the measures of their scales. For righteousness and the honored word of God are like one who fills [?].

And the poor, in turn, ponder on their beds. If the rich do not receive them, they become like a dry tree that has no moisture. Where there is no moisture, its root does not sprout, and when it has no root, no leaf sprouts.
And if no leaf sprouts, it produces no fruit, because the leaf serves the growth of the fruit. Whoever has no fruit has no good deeds, for a man's head is the fruit of righteousness.
And if he practices righteousness, he bears the fruit of uprightness. God rejoices in the person who practices righteousness and uprightness.
He grants the prayer of the one who prays and the reward of his lips. He does not oppress the righteous person because of the righteousness he has practiced.

And whoever declares a sinner righteous without repentance for the evil deeds he has done [?]. For God is righteous and loves righteousness. In judgment he shows favor neither to the rich nor to the poor, for he is the ruler of heaven and earth, and the life of everyone is in his hands.

He created the whole world out of nothing. He prepared and established the mountains and rocks, and made the earth firm upon the water. He enclosed it with sand so that it would not shake, for God's first word was, "Let there be light."
Light came into being while the world was in darkness. God did his work, preparing and establishing the world as was fitting and right, and he said, “Let there be evening and darkness.”
Again God said, “Let there be light,” and dawn broke and there was light. He raised the lower water above heaven.
He spread it out like sackcloth and supported it with wind. He made the lower [?] water dwell beneath the depths of the sea.

He closes the gates of the sea with sand and makes them firm by his spirit so that they do not sink into the depths below. He made wild beasts and animals dwell within it, and great animals within it, beyond counting, both those that are visible and those that are invisible.
On the third day God made plants upon the dry land, and all the grass and trees, each according to its kind, and the fruits they bear.

And the tree of life, beautiful to look at and sweet to eat, and grass and all the green plants of the earth that have their seed within them. He appointed them as food for all animals, wild beasts, and birds, and gave nourishment to everything he had created.

There was evening, and morning came. On the fourth day God said, "Let there be light in the expanse of heaven." God made the sun, the moon, and the stars, and placed them in the expanse of heaven to shine upon the earth and to rule over it by day and by night.
Then the sun, the moon, and the stars were created, and day and night.
On the fifth day God created all the wild beasts and animals [?] that live in the heavens, and all the birds that fly high in the air, and everything visible and invisible. God created all these.
On the sixth day he created all the wild beasts, livestock, and plants. After creating and arranging everything, he created Adam in his image and likeness.
He entrusted to him all the wild beasts and livestock he had created, so that he might rule over them, and also all the animals and wild beasts, the fish, and the leopards in the sea.
And the sheep, all the cattle upon the earth, and the animals that are visible and invisible.
He appointed the human being whom he had made in his image and likeness, and commanded him to eat, to cultivate the garden, and to praise God there.
And not to transgress God's command, and not to eat from the tree that imparts knowledge of good and evil, the tree of death.
For he said, “On the day you eat from this tree, you will surely die.”
Through the crafty one's deception, our mother Eve was ensnared. She ate from that tree and gave some to our father Adam.
He ate from that tree and brought death upon himself and his descendants.

God became angry with our father Adam because he had transgressed his command and eaten from the tree from which God had commanded him not to eat. He drove him out of the garden and gave him this land of thorns and thistles, which he had cursed because of him when he transgressed his command, so that he would cultivate it and eat the reward of his labor by the sweat of his face.
When God brought him out into this land, Adam fell into sorrow and anguish of heart. He began to cultivate the land and to eat by the sweat of his face, with hardship and toil.
Afterward, his children lived and multiplied. Among them were those who praised and honored God and did not transgress his command.

There were also prophets who prophesied what had happened and what would happen. And among the sinful children were those who lied and committed injustice. Cain, Adam's firstborn, became violent and killed his brother Abel.
Abel was righteous, but Cain became a sinner by killing his righteous brother Abel.
Then righteous Seth was born, for Adam fathered
Among them were prophets and righteous people, and among them were sinners and rebellious people.
Among them were good and blessed people who did the will of their father Adam and everything he told his son Seth, from Adam to righteous Noah, who kept God's commandment.

He too charged his children and told them God's will. They would tell their children and entrust them with God's will, just as their father Noah had told them, so that they would not stray from God's commandment.
They continued teaching their children who came after them.

But Satan fought against those who said yes to him, and spoke to them through idols at their fathers' tombs, idols in the form of images. They did everything that he, the teacher of evil, commanded them.
They worshiped idols according to their customs until righteous Abraham came forth, who did the will of God.
God's covenant was made with him in fire and in a whirlwind, because he was the first among his relatives to walk in the path of righteousness.
God swore to him that he would give him and his descendants a land as their inheritance forever.
Likewise, he made a covenant with Isaac to give him the inheritance of his father Abraham. He also made a covenant with Jacob to give him the inheritance of his father Isaac.
And their descendants after them, the children of Jacob, he made kings and priests from [?] the lineage of the people of Israel. He blessed them and said to them, "Increase and multiply abundantly."
He gave them their fathers' inheritance, but they did not stop provoking God, although he fed them and loved them in every way.
When he killed them, then they would seek him, turn back, and go to God, because God loved them and had mercy on them.
This was not for their own sake, but for their fathers' sake, because he is merciful and compassionate toward everything he has created.
He stretches out his right hand in blessing to satisfy the hungry soul. He opens his eyes in mercy and increases the grain for nourishment.
He gives food to young ravens and to all who call upon him. He also saves the children of Israel from the hands of their adversaries and enemies when they cry out to him.
But again they turn to provoking him, and he sends against them nations and their enemies who surround them. They destroy them, kill them, and take them captive.
Again they cry out to God with lamentation and tears, and he sends them help. Sometimes he saved them through the prophets.
At other times he saved them through the judges. When they provoked God, their enemies enslaved them, plundered them, and [?].
David arose and saved them from the power of the Philistines. Again they provoked God, and he sent against them those who would oppress them.

At one time he saved them through Jephthah. Again they forgot God, who had saved them, and he sent against them wicked enemies who tormented them, took them captive, and plundered them, for God was repaying them.
Again they cried out to him when they were oppressed, and he saved them through Gideon. Again they provoked God by the works of their hands.
He again sent them those who would torment them. They returned, wept, and cried out to God.
Again he saved them through Samson, and they rested for a short while. Then they arose to provoke God with the evil they had practiced before.
He again sent them others who would oppress them. Again they cried out and wept before God so that he would send them [?], and he saved them through Deborah and Barak.
Again they spent a few days worshiping God. Then they again forgot God and provoked him with their former evil.
He sent them others who would oppress them, and again he saved them through Judith. Again they remained for a little while, then arose to provoke God with their evil as before.
And he raised up for them men who would rule the nations. They cried out and pleaded with the Lord, and he saved them through Mattathias and his sons, on the corner of the house.

For he smashed the head of the giant Akemelek, who came to attack the land of Judah. When that giant died, his troops scattered and fled, and the children of Israel killed them until none survived or remained.

After this they rested for a little while, then rose up to provoke God. He sent nations to rule over them. Again they cried out and wailed to God, but he despised their weeping and their cries, because they continually provoked God and forgot his commandment.
They took them captive and carried them away to the land of the Chaldeans, together with their priests.
Even there the rebellious children of Israel did not stop provoking God. They made unclean things and idols, and joined with the nations that had taken them captive.

There too God was angered by their wickedness, so that he would destroy them all together. He brought wrath upon Artaxerxes, king of the Chaldeans, so that he would bring ten thousand denarii into the king's treasuries and condemn them on the appointed day, so that none of their descendants would remain in the land of Persia, from India to Ethiopia.
Thus he prepared a written message by the king's authority, and he gave him the seal that was on his hand, so that it would reach every city of Persia.

They were to kill them on a single day, as the king had commanded them, the day on which he wished to wipe them out. He ordered that their plunder, gold and silver, be brought into the king's treasuries.
At that time, when the children of Israel heard this, they cried out, wept, and wailed to God. They told Mordecai, and Mordecai told Esther.
Esther also said, “Fast, pray, and cry out to the Lord, the God of Israel, all you assemblies of the children of Israel, wherever you are.”
Mordecai also put on sackcloth and placed dust on his head. The children of Israel fasted, prayed, and repented wherever they were.

Esther mourned deeply. Although she was queen, she wore sackcloth, spread ashes, shaved her head, and did not anoint herself with perfume as the queens of Persia did. She wept and cried out from the depths of her heart to the Lord, the God of her ancestors.
Because of this, the Lord granted her favor before Artaxerxes, king of Persia, and she held a great feast for the God of her ancestors.
The king and Haman entered the banquet that Esther had prepared. There God repaid Haman according to what he had wanted to do to Mordecai, and they hanged him on a tall wooden pole.
The king’s written decree ordered that the Jews be left wherever they were, free to do as they wished, and that no one enslave them, drive them away, oppress them, or take their possessions.

They were not to destroy their towns or seize their livestock, but were to love and honor them wherever they were throughout the land of Persia. For this is how God shows mercy to Israel when they pray and cry out to him in repentance.

When they provoke him to anger, he sends nations against them to afflict them. Then they weep, cry out, and lament, asking him to send them help and save them from the hands of those who torment them.
And when the Egyptians afflicted the children of Israel with toil, oppressive labor, all the work they forced them to do, and making bricks without straw,
and appointed taskmasters over them and enslaved them, they cried out to God to save them from all the oppression of the Egyptians.

Then he sent them Moses and Aaron as their helpers, and they saved them from oppressive labor. For God sent them to bring his people out of the house of slavery belonging to Pharaoh, king of Egypt. In his pride, Pharaoh refused to release the people, so that they would not serve God or offer him sacrifices in the wilderness.
For God opposes the proud, and because of Pharaoh’s pride, God drowned him and his army in the Red Sea.

Likewise, there are kings and rulers who reject the word of God and do not act rightly in everything for which he appointed them and made them kings: to do his will and give their reward to those who serve well and honor his great name.
“If they establish my kingdom, I too will establish their kingdom,” says the Lord, who rules over all.
“Be good to me, and I too will be good to you. Keep my commandments, and I too will preserve your lives. Walk according to my commandments, and I too will act according to your hearts’ desires.
Love me, and I too will love your lives. Take refuge in me, and I too will strengthen you.
Trust in me, and I too will save you,” says the Lord who rules over all.

“Do not wander this way and that. Draw near to me, and I will draw you near, for I love upright paths,” says the Lord who rules over all. “Cleanse your hands, you sinners and evildoers, and remove the evil from your hearts.
And I too will remove my wrath from you and turn toward you with compassion and mercy.”

“I will keep hostile rebels who commit injustice far from you, just as I saved my servant David from the many [?] that befell him: from the hand of Goliath the giant, from the hand of Saul, who sought to kill him, and from the hand of his son Absalom, who wanted to seize his kingdom.

Likewise, I will save those who do my will, keep my commandments, and persevere in my law. I will give them glory as their inheritance and make them reign above all, so that they may rejoice both in this world and in the world to come.
They will share with the blessed kings who pleased God through the goodness of their lives, like Samuel, whom God chose while he was still a child, because of the goodness of his life.
And he spoke, as he spoke to Eli, the elderly priest whose conduct was good, and to Samuel the prophet while he served in the house of the Lord God.

When he grew up serving in the house of the Lord, he appointed him to appoint the people and anoint kings at the Lord’s command. He entrusted the royal anointing to his hands when he did the will of the Lord his God, because he was pleasing in his sight, so that he might establish kings over the people whom the Lord had chosen from the children of Israel.
While Saul was reigning, the Lord said to Samuel the prophet, “Go and anoint David, the son of Jesse, from the house of Judah, for I am pleased with him.
I have hated the house of Saul, because he provoked me by transgressing my word.
And I too have rejected him. No one from his house will reign again, because he did not keep my word.
Likewise, from those who have not kept my word and do not walk according to my law and my ordinances, I will withhold my gifts, and I will withhold my kingdom from their descendants forever.
I will change my mind and not exalt them again, but will only destroy them. For when I exalted them, they did not exalt me, and when I honored them, they did not honor me.
When I was good to them, they were not good to me, and when I showed them mercy, they did not show me mercy.
For I made them the head over everyone, but they did not make me the head over them. When I honored them above everyone, they did not honor me or keep my commandments.

I have also taken away the gift that I gave them, and I will not return it to them, just as I swore in my anger. Whoever honors me, I will honor; and whoever loves me, I will love.” Thus says the Lord, who rules over all.
“But those who do not honor me and have not kept my commandments, I will deprive of the gift that I gave them.
The Lord, who rules over all, says, “Whoever loves me, I will love; and whoever exalts me, I will exalt.
For [?] the Lord, who rules over all, and no one can rescue from my hand, in heaven above or on earth below. For I am the Lord, who kills and gives life, who punishes and shows mercy.
Greatness and glory are mine. Whoever I love, I will honor; and whoever I hate, I will humiliate.
I am the one who shows compassion to those who love me and remember my name at all times. For the poor and the rich, I am the provider of food.
This applies not only to human beings, but also to livestock, birds, wild animals, fish in the sea, and [?],
and to leopards, crocodiles, [?], Behemoth, and frogs.
Everything that moves in the water and everything that flies above [?] is mine.
I am the one who provides what is fitting and desired for all those who seek me.
Kings are not appointed without my will; the poor do not become destitute without my command; and the mighty do not become strong without my will.
I gave favor to David and wisdom to Solomon, and I added years to Hezekiah’s life.
I shortened Goliath’s days, and I gave strength to Samson and then weakened his strength.
I saved my servant David from the hand of Goliath the giant.”
And again from the hand of King Saul, and again from the hand of another giant who opposed him, and from the hands of all who opposed him and fought against him, because he kept my commandment.
And I loved him. I also love all the kings and rulers who keep my commandments, and I give them strength and victory over their enemies, because they too have made me glad.
And again I will give them the land as an inheritance, which I swore to their fathers—a pure and radiant land—so that they may inherit the land of their fathers.

And you, kings and rulers, listen to my word and keep my commandments,” says the Lord who rules over all. “The children of Israel rebelled against me and worshiped other gods, although I am the Lord their God, who protected them, saved them, made them greater than their ancestors, and fed them with everything they desired.

I raised them up over the might of the earth and nourished them with the earth’s blessing, and, as was fitting, with vineyards they had not planted, olive oil, and cisterns of sweet water they had not dug.
And [?] of honey and sheep’s milk, together with fine wheat flour, embroidered clothes, and everything they desired.
And I withheld from them nothing that they asked of me.
I also fed them manna, bread in the wilderness, as David said, ‘Human beings ate the bread of his angels.’ I did all this for them so that they would worship me in righteousness and uprightness.
But they did not worship me, and I too despised them,” says the Lord who rules over all. “They rebelled against me and walked on a path that was not mine.

I too will repay them according to their conduct, and I have despised them according to the work of their hands, because they despised worshiping me and did not persevere in my ordinances and my counsel. I will bring them down under the condemnation of the judgment in heaven.
On earth too I will shorten their days, because they did not keep my commandments, and I too will rebel against them.
And you, king, are you not a human being who will die and decay, who tomorrow will become moths and worms and dust?
And now you boast and grow proud, as though you will never die.
But you are a human being who now appears alive and tomorrow is dead, says the Lord who rules over all.

But if you keep my word and my commandments, I will give you the holy city as an inheritance, together with those who have done my will: honored kings whose dwellings are radiant, whose crowns are beautiful, and whose thrones of gold and silver are set in place for them to sit upon.
And you will rejoice in his city, which is a nearby dwelling for those who do good.
But those who do evil are not fit to enter that city into which honored kings enter.
For they did not keep my word and my ordinances, says the Lord who rules over all.
The kingdom of the Medes will perish, but the kingdom of Rome will become stronger than the kingdom of Macedonia, the kingdom of Nineveh, and the kingdom of Persia.
And the kingdom of Ethiopia against the kingdom of Alexandria, and the kingdom of Moab against Amalek, for they will rise up.
Brother will rise against brother, and the Lord will exact vengeance, as he said concerning them, so that they perish.
And he said, “Kingdom will rise against kingdom, nation against nation, and city against city.”
There will be itching, killing, famine, pestilence, upheaval, and [?] of winter, because peace and love have departed, and the Lord’s scourge has descended upon it.
And when the day of the Lord draws near, suddenly, like lightning that appears from east to west.

Then everyone will be repaid according to his deeds, according to the labor of his hands, and according to the fruit of his deeds. For the Lord himself said that on the day of judgment he will take vengeance upon them, and at that time their feet will slip, because the day of their destruction has drawn near.
In that year the Lord will destroy, in eternal judgment, those who do evil and have not walked according to his law: the people of Judah, Cyprus, Samaria, Damascus, and the people of Babylon.
And those who live on the islands of Arabia, India, Nubia, Sheba, Egypt, and Ethiopia, and all who live on them.
Then they will know that I am the Lord who rules heaven and earth, and that I am the one who gives honor and favor, and I am the one who kills and gives life.
And I am the one who makes the sun rise and sends it to its setting, and I am the one who brings good and evil.
And I am the one who brings a people you do not know, who will consume the fruit of your labor and the pastures of your cattle and sheep.

They will [?] your children before you and take them captive, and you will be unable to save them. They will consume the fruits of your toil and your lush growth, because you did not fear the commandment of the Lord that you heard, because the Spirit of the Lord did not increase upon you.
But the one upon whom the Spirit of the Lord rests knows everything, as Nebuchadnezzar said to the prophet Daniel, “For I see the Spirit of the Lord upon you.”

For the one who has the Spirit of the Lord knows everything; even what is hidden becomes revealed to him. Nothing is hidden from the Spirit of the Lord, but he knows everything, both hidden and revealed.
For we are human beings; tomorrow we die, and our hidden deeds will be revealed—everything we have done.
As gold and silver are tested by fire, so sinners will be tested on the last day, because they did not keep the commandment of the Lord.
Then the deeds of all the children of Israel and of all the nations will be put to the test.
Woe to you, mighty men of Israel, for the Lord is angry with you because you have not administered justice properly for mortals.
Woe to you who go to the tavern morning and evening, become drunk, and plunder, and do not listen to the plea for justice of mortals and the poor, while you sit amid wedding festivities and luxury.
Thus the Lord said to the mighty men of Israel: “Woe to you if you do not walk according to my commandments, keep my word, and love what I desire.”
And I too will bring scourging, wasting, and sickness upon you, and you will perish like food consumed by locusts and caterpillars. No trace of you will be found within your borders.

Your city will become a wilderness, and everyone who once saw it will clap his hands and mock it, saying, “Is this not the city that was filled with blessings and every good thing? Has God made it like this because of the wickedness of those who live in it?”

Woe to her! She grew proud in her heart, raised her head, and stiffened her neck, until God humbled her to the dust of the earth because of the pride of those who live in her. She became a wilderness, and thorns and thistles grew over her.
It became a place of confusion and desolation; it became [?] and a wilderness, and wild beasts dwell within it.

She became a terror to those who pass through her, because the wrath of God fell upon her. She drank from the cup of his wrath because of the pride of her heart and the wickedness of those who inhabit her.
Do not boast, Macedonians, and do not proudly raise your necks, Amalekites, for there is a God who will take vengeance upon you.
For you rise as high as heaven, but you will descend into Sheol.
And at the time of Israel’s first entry into the land of Egypt, under the rule of the [?] and the Moabites, he said, “Do not boast, for it is not fitting for you to reproach God as you do.”

And you too, Ishmaelite, son of a slave woman, why do you stretch out your neck toward what is not yours? Do you not remember that God will judge you on the day of judgment, when he rises to judge the earth?
Then you will be repaid according to the work of your hands. Why do you exalt your heart and stretch out your neck? says the Lord who rules over all.
And I too will reproach you just as you reproached those who are not yours, even where I sent you, because you choose to do evil.
And I too will do the same to you, says God, who rules over everything. But if you do good and love what I love, I too will listen to you in everything you ask of me.
I will do what you desire if you do what I desire. Your adversary will not stand against you, and I will bless your work, your seed, and your children.

I will bless the pasture of your cattle and your sheep, and I will bless everything to which you put your hand, if you walk according to my commandments and do what I love, says God, who rules over everything.

But if you do not do what I desire and do not walk according to my commandments and my judgments, all this judgment of mine that was spoken of earlier will overtake you. You will not be able to escape my wrath, which will come upon you at all times, because you did not conduct yourself according to my commandments or walk according to my judgments.
You did not prefer what I prefer, and you turned aside from praising and worshiping me, although I created you when you did not exist.

I gave you honor and glory among the people who are beneath you, so that you might do whatever you wished: you kill and [?], you build and tear down, you honor and humiliate, you exalt and bring low. This is yours.
If you do the will of the Lord and walk in his commandments, he will love you, so that you may rejoice with him in his kingdom and have a share with those who have inherited the holy city.

For he said, “If they obey me, I will give them honor and favor as their inheritance, and I will make them rejoice in my house of prayer. They will be chosen and accepted like a sacrificial offering,” says God, who rules over everything.
Do not be reluctant to do good and follow the path of salvation, so that you may pass from death into life.
As for those who persist in doing good, God will shelter them in every good thing, so that they may be his servants, like Job, whom God protected from every evil.

And like Abraham, whom he saved when he was killing the kings, and as he saved Moses from the hand of Pharaoh and from the hands of the Canaanites among whom Abraham lived, while they sought his life evening and morning, day and night, to bring him down among their idols.
But he endured, refusing them concerning their carved images while they dragged him.
And he refused them and feared God, who created him, for God was Abraham’s refuge, in whom he had trusted from his youth.

He did not diminish his worship of God until the year of his death, for he loved God exceedingly. He did not depart from his commandment until the day of his death, and he taught his children to keep God’s commandment.

And they too did not depart from his commandment, following what their father had done. Abraham’s descendants, his servants Isaac and Jacob, did not depart from God’s commandment. Concerning them God spoke, saying to his angels, “I have a friend
on earth: Abraham, my beloved, and Isaac, my child, and Jacob, in whom my soul delights. Through them I have been glorified,” says God, who rules over everything.
And the children of Israel continually provoked him all the more, while he [?] them and fed them manna in the wilderness.
Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not crack, because they were fed with manna, which is the bread of knowledge.
But their hearts continually turn away from God, and they have no hope of salvation, because they have been evildoers from the beginning.

They were not like their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who pleased God by the goodness of their lives. Instead, they became like a crooked bow and continually provoked him with their idols, their [?], and their sacred mountains. They ate among the mountains, among the trees, and among the rocks.
They slaughtered animals, offered sacrifices, and rejoiced in the work of their hands. They ate sacrificial meat and drank the wine of their drink offerings, and they sang and danced with demons.
The demons delighted them with all their singing and dancing, all their drunkenness, unrestrained sexual immorality, greed, and oppression, in which God takes no pleasure.
They sacrificed to the idol of Canaan, to Baal, to Marya of Midian, and to the idols of the Philistines: Dagon, Apollo, Artemis, and Ratsion [?].

They worshiped all the gods of the nations around them, doing everything as the nations did, according to what they saw and heard, including all the dancing, singing, and festivities practiced by the nations.

The people of Israel did the same, though they said, “We worship God.” They did not carry out his law and his commandment, which Moses told them in the Torah: that they should keep God's commandments and refrain from worshiping idols,

and should not worship foreign gods besides the God of their ancestors, who fed them with the grain of the fields, brought them up onto the heights of the earth, satisfied them with honey from the rock, and fed them with manna.
He did not withhold from them what they desired and wanted, because he was their God, and he fed them with what they wanted.
But they did not stop provoking God, and when he made them happy, they forgot God.
When he punished them, they cried out to him, and he saved them from the distress that had overtaken them. Then they again rejoiced openly and lived for many days.
Then they changed their hearts and returned to provoking God as before. He raised up against them the nations around them to kill them, enslave them, and afflict them.
And again they will return and set out and cry out to the Lord their God.

Yet he had mercy on them, not for their own sake, but for the sake of their ancestors, with whom he had sworn an oath and established his covenant: Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, who long ago pleased God by the goodness of their lives.
He loved those who loved him and kept his commandment, so that he would multiply their descendants like the sand of the sea and like the stars of heaven.
By saying “like the sand of the sea,” he meant the sinful souls among the children of Israel who will enter the sea of fire at the resurrection of the dead.

But the souls of the righteous from the descendants of the children of Israel are like bright stars in the heights of heaven. For the Lord said to Abraham, “Look at the sky at night and count the stars of heaven, if you can count them. In the same way, your righteous descendants will shine like stars in the kingdom of heaven.”

Again he said to him, “Look into the sea and at the banks of the river, and see what is in the sand. Count them, if you can count their number. So will your descendants be who descend into hell at the resurrection of the dead.”
Abraham believed in God, and because of this he was righteous. His hope was fulfilled on earth, and after his wife Sarah had grown old, she bore a son, Isaac.
He will also receive a kingdom in heaven because of his faith, for he believed that the dead would rise and that those who had done good would enter eternal life,
and those who had done evil would enter eternal condemnation at the resurrection of the dead. The righteous, who have done good, will reign with him forever and ever.
Those who have done evil will be condemned forever and ever. Amen and amen.
